evidence.quote: In Petaurista and Aeroiuvs, the tail is more or less narrow and round, and there is a well-developed interfemoral membrane present; in the remainder, so far as seen, there is no well-developed interfemoral membrane, and the tail is wider, flatter, having an appearance very much like a large feather.

interfemoral_membrane.notes: Well-developed interfemoral membrane (uropatagium). Coded under both existing keys (interfemoral_membrane, interfemoral_membrane_well_developed) so north- and south-group genera are comparable. Ellerman 1940: only Petaurista and Aeromys (of the genera he saw) have a well-developed interfemoral membrane.

upper_incisor_groove.notes: Inferred from the HMW (2016) genus-level statement that grooved upper incisors distinguish Aeretes from Petaurista and all other flying-squirrel genera (HMW 2016 composition included the species now in this genus, e.g. Priapomys leonardi within Hylopetes, Olisthomys morrisi within Petinomys setosus, H. electilis within H. phayrei). No source describes a groove on the front face of the upper incisors in this genus.

zygomatic_plate_high_tilted.notes: Ellerman 1940 Hylopetes account ("primitive, of Belomys type, not high"); Ellerman's Hylopetes did not include H. bartelsi, H. electilis, H. sipora or H. winstoni (and did include leonardi, now Priapomys), hence partial.

Hylopetes.distinguishing_notes: Separators found (scope genus/species-union unless stated): vs Aeretes - upper_incisor_groove (smooth vs grooved; HMW 2016) and upper_molar_posterior_flexus_distinct (no vs yes; Li et al. 2021, McKenna 1962). vs Belomys and vs Trogopterus - upper_cheekteeth_hypocone_distinct (no vs yes; Li et al. 2021) and cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled (no vs yes; Thomas 1908, Ellerman 1940). vs Petaurista - interfemoral_membrane / interfemoral_membrane_well_developed (not vs well developed; Ellerman 1940) and posterior flexus (no vs yes). vs Pteromys - coronoid_process_reduced (no vs yes; Li et al. 2021 key couplet 2) and metaloph_notched_separate_metaconule (no vs yes). vs Olisthomys - bullar_septa / bulla_septa_honeycomb (<4 vs >4 septa; Li et al. 2021 key, Kruskop et al. 2022, McKenna 1962). NOT separable at full-genus scope: vs Eoglaucomys and vs Priapomys. Li et al. 2021 key couplet 10 (distinct mesoloph, four buccal cusps) separates most Hylopetes from both, but H. nigripes and H. bartelsi lack the mesoloph/mesostyle. Table S6 characters separate the 8 Hylopetes species examined (partial): vs Eoglaucomys upper_m3_metaloph (absent vs reduced); vs Priapomys upper_molar_anterior_flexus (present vs absent) and glans length (long vs very long, one H. alboniger specimen). H. winstoni (one specimen) was never examined.

upper_incisor_groove.notes: Inferred from the HMW (2016) genus-level statement that grooved upper incisors distinguish Aeretes from Petaurista and all other flying-squirrel genera (HMW 2016 composition included the species now in this genus, e.g. Priapomys leonardi within Hylopetes, Olisthomys morrisi within Petinomys setosus, H. electilis within H. phayrei). No source describes a groove on the front face of the upper incisors in this genus.

bulla_septa_honeycomb.notes: Binary version of bullar_septa: yes = more than 4 internal bullar septa (Li et al. 2021 honeycomb form, and also their cobweb form in Petinomys, which likewise has >4 septa); no = fewer than 4 (common form). More than 4 septa: Li et al. 2021 score their P. setosus sample (which includes the Olisthomys holotype AMNH 113031) as honeycomb; McKenna 1962: six septa, the posterior ones "of the multiple anastomosing type" (anastomosing = joined/crossing, closer to Li's cobweb form); Kruskop et al. 2022: about six simple septa. Both >4 states kept.

Olisthomys.distinguishing_notes: vs Hylopetes: bullar_septa / bulla_septa_honeycomb (>4 septa vs <4).

evidence.quote: The tails of Iomys Thomas , Hylopetes Thomas , Petinomys Thomas , and Petaurillus Thomas are distinctly distichous and there is no interfemoral membrane.

interfemoral_membrane.notes: Well-developed interfemoral membrane (uropatagium). Coded under both existing keys (interfemoral_membrane, interfemoral_membrane_well_developed) so north- and south-group genera are comparable. Ellerman 1940: only Petaurista and Aeromys (of the genera he saw) have a well-developed interfemoral membrane. Sanamxay et al. 2013 (comparison with Biswamoyopterus): no interfemoral membrane in this genus.

upper_incisor_groove.notes: Inferred from the HMW (2016) genus-level statement that grooved upper incisors distinguish Aeretes from Petaurista and all other flying-squirrel genera (HMW 2016 composition included the species now in this genus, e.g. Priapomys leonardi within Hylopetes, Olisthomys morrisi within Petinomys setosus, H. electilis within H. phayrei). No source describes a groove on the front face of the upper incisors in this genus.

caveats:
PURPOSE: follow-up harmonising Pteromyini characters across all 17 MDD v2.5 genera under one set of keys. Existing keys reused with their existing state names: ear_base_tufts, bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb, coronoid_process_reduced, upper_molar_posterior_flexus_distinct, upper_cheekteeth_hypocone_distinct, interfemoral_membrane AND interfemoral_membrane_well_developed (both coded with identical evidence so that north- and south-file genera become comparable), cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled, upper_cheekteeth_quadricuspidate, upper_premolars, upper_incisor_groove. New keys (Li et al. 2021 Table S6 columns / key couplets): upper_cheekteeth_mesostyle, upper_cheekteeth_mesolophule, upper_cheekteeth_anterolophule, upper_cheekteeth_paraconule, upper_cheekteeth_metaconule, upper_m3_metaloph, upper_molar_anterior_flexus, upper_molar_central_flexus, lower_cheekteeth_hypoconulid, lower_cheekteeth_protolophid_entolophid, metaloph_notched_separate_metaconule, glans_penis_length_class, zygomatic_plate_high_tilted.

QUOTES: every quote was machine-checked (whitespace-normalised substring) against the retrieved texts before writing. Li et al. 2021 Table S6 was re-extracted from the COMPLETE supplementary PDF (scratchpad/pn/supp/zr-42-4-389-S1.pdf, 27 pages) with pdftotext -raw; row quotes are the raw-text rows joined with single spaces, so multi-line cells appear in pdftotext order (e.g. "Hylopetes P mostly P, mostly P, mostly R ... A A connect to mesolophule connect to mesostyle"). Cell-to-column assignment was taken from the layout-preserving rendering (pn/supp/zr-42-4-389-S1.txt) and checked token-by-token against the raw rows. OCR errors in Ellerman 1940, Thomas 1908, Allen 1940 and HMW/Plazi texts are preserved (e.g. "offlying", "upperincisors", "Aeroiuvs", "wrink- ling").

TABLE S6 SEMANTICS: "mostly X" = a few exceptional individuals differ but their state is not given, so ALL states are recorded for such cells; "A or R" = both. R ("reduced, obsolete, but recognizable") is counted as present for presence/absence characters. Li et al.'s "ear tufts" are basal ear tufts and are coded as ear_base_tufts (not the brief's ear-tip ear_tufts).

SCOPE: Table S6-derived codings are scope "genus" only where Li et al.'s specimen list covers every MDD v2.5 species (Aeretes, Aeromys, Belomys, Biswamoyopterus, Eoglaucomys, Eupetaurus, Glaucomys, Iomys, Petinomys, Priapomys, Pteromys, Pteromyscus, Trogopterus). They are "partial" for Hylopetes (H. winstoni never examined; H. sipora skin only; H. bartelsi skull only; H. electilis examined as skulls filed under H. phayrei: AMNH M-58161/58171/58179, identified as H. electilis from Hainan in AMNH/GBIF records), Petaurillus (P. emiliae not examined), Petaurista (P. marica, P. siangensis, P. nujiangensis not in the specimen list). Statements from Li et al.'s "Key to the genera of living flying squirrels", the Priapomys diagnosis, McKenna 1962, Ellerman 1940, Kruskop et al. 2022 and HMW 2016 that are phrased about a genus as a whole are scope "genus" (notes flag where the source's genus concept lacked an MDD species, chiefly H. winstoni). ASSUMPTION: earlier files' "partial"/"unknown" codings are treated by the importer as no information (as current_codings suggests); if the importer instead expands partial to all states, Hylopetes bullar_septa (partial in pteromyini_south.json) would cancel the Hylopetes-Olisthomys separation.

OLISTHOMYS: Li et al. 2021 pooled O. morrisi in Petinomys setosus; their P. setosus sample includes AMNH 113031 (skull, teeth), the holotype of Pteromys (Olisthomys) morrisi Carter 1942. Only Petinomys-row cells without a modifier (true of every examined specimen, hence of AMNH 113031) were transferred to Olisthomys, as species-union. Kruskop et al. 2022's Vietnam specimen (outside the MDD v2.5 range of O. morrisi) is used only as partial or as supporting evidence.

CONFLICTS kept as unions: Eupetaurus hypocone (Li: distinct; McKenna: merged) and posterior flexus (Li: central flexus only; McKenna: enlarged posterolingual diagonal flexus); Eupetaurus paraconule (Table S6 very D vs key couplet 9 indistinct); Pteromyscus paraconule (Table S6 R vs key 9 distinct); Aeromys mesostyle (Table S6 present vs McKenna none); Aeromys hypocone (Li yes here; McKenna no in pteromyini_south.json); Petaurista cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled (Ellerman key yes vs McKenna "low and simple" in P. leucogenys); Biswamoyopterus upper_incisor_groove (HMW implies smooth; B. laoensis has "a deep groove on the inner margin"); Petaurista upper_incisor_groove (faint grooves in individuals). Petaurista ear_base_tufts was not re-coded (pteromyini_north.json already has both states).

UPPER INCISOR GROOVE: "smooth" for 13 genera is an inference from HMW 2016's statement that grooved upper incisors distinguish Aeretes from Petaurista and all other flying-squirrel genera (supported for Petaurista and Eupetaurus by McKenna 1962). No direct description of incisor front faces was found for most genera.

PAIR RESULTS (simulated union of north + south + this file, ignoring partial/unknown): Hylopetes-Aeretes: upper_incisor_groove, upper_molar_posterior_flexus_distinct. Hylopetes-Belomys: upper_cheekteeth_hypocone_distinct, cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled, bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Hylopetes-Eoglaucomys: NONE at full-genus scope (Table S6 upper_m3_metaloph absent vs reduced and Ellerman's zygomatic plate separate only partially: 8/10 Hylopetes species, resp. Hylopetes sensu Ellerman). Hylopetes-Olisthomys: bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Hylopetes-Petaurista: interfemoral_membrane(+_well_developed), upper_molar_posterior_flexus_distinct. Hylopetes-Petinomys: bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Hylopetes-Priapomys: NONE at full-genus scope (key couplet 10 fails for H. nigripes and H. bartelsi; Table S6 upper_molar_anterior_flexus present vs absent and glans length long vs very long cover only the Hylopetes species examined). Hylopetes-Pteromys: coronoid_process_reduced, metaloph_notched_separate_metaconule. Hylopetes-Trogopterus: upper_cheekteeth_hypocone_distinct, cheekteeth_excessively_wrinkled, bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Aeromys-Petaurista: upper_molar_posterior_flexus_distinct only. Belomys-Petinomys: hypocone, wrinkling, paraconule, M3 metaloph, hypoconulid, protolophid/entolophid, anterior and central flexus. Belomys-Pteromyscus: ear_base_tufts, lower_cheekteeth_protolophid_entolophid. Petaurista-Petinomys: interfemoral membrane, posterior flexus, bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Petaurista-Pteromyscus: interfemoral membrane, posterior flexus, hypocone, bullar_septa, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Petinomys-Priapomys: bullar_septa, ear_base_tufts, bulla_septa_honeycomb. Biswamoyopterus-Petinomys: hypocone, interfemoral membrane, anterior and central flexus. No previously separable Pteromyini pair lost its separation through the added states.
